name: Cursed
label: Deathwish
lede: Three albums titled with Roman numerals, one very loud van, and a band that ended in a Dutch club with the tour money gone.

eras.title: After The Swarm
eras.text: Chris Colohan had just finished with The Swarm and had already been through Left for Dead and Ruination. Cursed was built across a few cities from people he already knew, with the goal of playing hardcore slower, heavier and meaner.

years.h: The Swarm ends. Chris Colohan starts Cursed
years.p: [[Chris Colohan|f1494c0a-331d-45dd-a51c-6c43d43ccc69]] forms Cursed with Christian McMaster on guitar and Mike Maxymuik on drums, plus Radwan Ghazi Moumneh, formerly of the Quebec band Ire.
years.xp:
Wikipedia places the founding in 2001, a year after The Swarm (also known as Knee Deep in the Dead) broke up. Colohan had earlier sung in [[Left for Dead|cd47905f-3117-4bb2-9291-c258b240ef7d]], and Maxymuik had played with him in Ruination.

Colohan told Lambgoat the band started in winter 2001/02, with him and Moumneh in Montreal and McMaster and Maxymuik in Ontario. Moumneh started on bass.

years.h: A self-released demo, recorded across two provinces
years.p: Cursed put out a self-released demo in 2002 while the band was still split between Montreal and Ontario.

years.cap: Cursed in their early days. Photo credit to be confirmed.
years.h: Five days at Chemical Sound with Kurt Ballou
years.p: Cursed record their first album at Chemical Sound in Toronto, October 19-23, 2002, with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] producing.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the session dates and Ballou as producer. It came out on Deathwish Inc., the label run by Ballou's Converge bandmate [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]].

eras.title: I, II, and a wrecked amp
eras.text: The debut on Deathwish gave the band a cult following, then a second album in a real studio cleaned up the noise without softening it. Lineup turnover on bass was the only real instability.

years.p: Released February 25, 2003: twelve tracks in about 32 minutes, opening with "Polygraph" and stretching to nearly seven minutes on "Opposable Thumbs".

years.h: Moumneh moves to guitar, Tom Piraino takes bass
years.p: Tom "Dot Com" Piraino, who had played with McMaster in Funerary, joined on bass while Moumneh became the second guitarist.
A demo of the title track backed with a cover of The Stooges' "Search and Destroy", pressed as 2,000 copies in several colors.
years.xp:
Hex Records' owner says he promised it would be a one-time pressing and never repressed. The title track was later re-recorded for II.

Colohan told the label's retrospective the song was about the blowback of exporting dominance and greed after 9/11. He also said it took a year of lining up their lives to be able to tour.

q: Two is the first thing we're all pretty much totally happy with.
years.h: II on Goodfellow Records, mixed by Ian Blurton
years.p: Released January 25, 2005, 34 minutes long, with "Model Home Invasion" and "Head of the Baptist" among the eleven tracks.
years.xp: Ian Blurton produced it at Chemical Sound on analog gear, a step up from the self-produced debut. Colohan told Exclaim!, "Two is the first thing we're all pretty much totally happy with." Reviewers at Punknews, PopMatters and Lambgoat covered it, and Wikipedia says most were positive.

years.h: Dan Dunham replaces Piraino on bass
years.p: Dunham, who also played in Shallow, North Dakota, held the bass spot until the end in 2008.

eras.title: Volume machismo
eras.text: The band's live show was known for extreme volume, and it produced at least one on-record injury. Compilations and reissues kept the catalog moving while the third album was written.

years.h: Colohan gets electrocuted while filming a video
years.p: Exclaim! reported the band had toned down its amp stacks after incidents including Colohan being shocked during a video shoot.
A compilation titled Fatalist appeared in 2006, collecting Cursed material outside the albums.

years.h: I reissued on gatefold vinyl; Blackout at Sunrise picture disc
years.p: Trash Art! repressed the debut as a 180-gram gatefold, and the band issued the Blackout at Sunrise picture-disc EP.

eras.title: Architects, then a robbery
eras.text: The third album was the band's biggest release, then the European tour to support it ended in Amsterdam and the band never played again.

years.cap: Cover art by John Baizley of Baroness.
years.h: III: Architects of Troubled Sleep closes the trilogy
years.p: Eleven tracks from "Architects of Troubled Sleep" to "Gutters", released on Goodfellow in North America, Howling Bull in Japan and Reflections in Europe.
years.xp: It was recorded at Hallamusic in Toronto, mixed by Donny Cooper and mastered by Alan Douches, with cover art by [[Baroness|eeb41a1e-4326-4d04-8c47-0f564ceecd68]] frontman John Baizley. Deathwish later pressed it on vinyl in an edition of Silver, White/Black mix and Clear with Brown splatter, and called it the band's hardest-hitting album.

years.h: Sold-out Lee's Palace release show in Toronto
years.p: Cursed played six weekends of Southern Ontario DIY shows before the album came out. The release show at Lee's Palace, with 50Watthead, Career Suicide and Living Darkness, was sold out.

q: A bullet in the head, the end of the line.
years.h: Robbed in Europe, done in Amsterdam
years.p: On May 22, 2008, Colohan wrote from Germany that the band had been robbed of passports, money and tour funds. Cursed played a last show at Bitterzoet in Amsterdam.
years.xp:
Exclaim! quoted Colohan calling it a bullet in the head, the end of the line, and a sudden and totally fucked up way for a band to end. He said they would play the show, badly, and go their separate ways.

He also said the tour, apart from the last chaotic shows, had been their best, and that all outstanding plans were off. Colohan went to Prague afterward.

eras.title: What came next
eras.text: Colohan turned the catalog into a small archive, then kept playing in other bands. Members ended up in Montreal's experimental scene and other groups.

years.h: The Last Session EP on High Anxiety
years.p: Colohan released Cursed's final UK radio session as a 7" on his own vinyl-only High Anxiety label.

years.h: Colohan, Maxymuik, Dunham and Moumneh move on
years.p: Colohan played in [[Burning Love|47ad0632-61da-455b-9674-a159b3eea43e]] and Mature Situations; Maxymuik joined Quest for Fire and toured with Pink Mountaintops; Dunham played in Crux of Aux, Skull and Limitoids.
years.xp: Moumneh co-opened Hotel2Tango in Montreal with people from Godspeed You! Black Emperor and Constellation Records, and continues the performance project Jerusalem in My Heart.

years.h: Colohan forms SECT with Andy Hurley of Fall Out Boy
years.p: The new band had Hurley on drums, with James Chang and Scott Crouse on guitar and Ian Edwards on bass.

years.h: Deathwish presses A Young Person's Guide to Cursed on 8-track
years.p: The label put 30 tracks from all three albums on a handmade 90-minute cassette and called Cursed a very important band to Deathwish.
